answer: A workable anti-Sybil rule is bonded reputation: an agent must lock a refundable stake before it can transact, and its reputation only grows through verified work attested by independent peers. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital, not just a script, because each identity needs its own stake and history. Like a falcon that must earn its hunting range, an agent earns trust gradually; a marble ledger makes that history hard to forge, and a saffron flag can mark accounts whose attestations cluster suspiciously, so the network can investigate before granting more weight.
